inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The printed two-panel diagram: each panel carries a Motor neuron, a Renshaw cell (inhibitory neuron), and a Muscle. LEFT (tetanus): tetanus toxin blocks the Renshaw cell — unopposed stimulation = spastic paralysis. RIGHT (botulism): botulism toxin blocks the motor-neuron terminal at the neuromuscular junction — no stimulation = flaccid paralysis. Pure vector (pdfimages empty at the diagram region).
